san-peoples.name: San people
san-peoples.summary: Indigenous hunter-gatherer peoples of southern Africa and among the oldest surviving cultures in the region, with ancestry possibly diverging from other humans 100,000 to 200,000 years ago.

khoekhoe.name: Khoekhoe
khoekhoe.summary: Traditionally nomadic pastoralist indigenous peoples of Southern Africa, once called Hottentots, who by the 17th century kept large cattle herds in the Cape region before mostly abandoning nomadic herding in the 19th–20th centuries.

sao-civilisation.name: Sao civilization
sao-civilisation.summary: A civilization that flourished by the Chari River in Central Africa from around 2000 BC to the 16th century AD, the earliest known culture in modern Chad and Cameroon.

chari-river.name: Chari River
chari-river.summary: A 1,400-kilometre river in Central Africa and the main source of water for Lake Chad.

nilo-saharan-languages.name: Nilo-Saharan languages
nilo-saharan-languages.summary: A proposed family of around 210 African languages spoken by roughly 70 million people mainly around the upper Nile and Chari rivers, named by linguist Joseph Greenberg in 1963.

sara-people.name: Sara people
sara-people.summary: A Central Sudanic ethnic group native to southern Chad and nearby areas, forming roughly 30% of Chad's population and historically organized into patrilineal clans.

sotho-people.name: Sotho
sotho-people.summary: A Sotho-Tswana ethnic group of Southern Africa, whose ancestors are believed to have migrated south from Northeast Africa around the fifth century AD.

khoisan.name: Khoisan
khoisan.summary: An umbrella term for Southern Africa's non-Bantu indigenous peoples, combining the Khoekhoen and Sān, who speak click languages and descend from some of the earliest modern human populations in the region.

bantu-expansion.name: Bantu expansion
bantu-expansion.summary: A series of prehistoric migrations, roughly 4000 BCE to 500 CE, of Bantu-speaking peoples from West-Central Africa across Central, Eastern and Southern Africa.

urewe.name: Urewe culture
urewe.summary: Early Iron Age culture of the Lake Victoria region of Africa, with sites dating from the 5th century BC to the 6th century AD. Its earliest dated artefacts are in Tanzania's Kagera Region.

christopher-ehret.name: Christopher Ehret
christopher-ehret.summary: American scholar of African history and historical linguistics (1941–2025), a UCLA professor for nearly fifty years known for linking language reconstruction with the archaeological record.

kwazulu-natal.name: KwaZulu-Natal
kwazulu-natal.summary: A South African province created in 1994 by merging the Zulu bantustan of KwaZulu with Natal Province; it includes Durban and was once home to the independent Zulu Kingdom.

limpopo.name: Limpopo Province
limpopo.summary: The northernmost province of South Africa, named after the Limpopo River, formed in 1994 from former Bantustans and part of the old Transvaal province.

great-zimbabwe.name: Great Zimbabwe
great-zimbabwe.summary: A city in south-eastern Zimbabwe settled around 1000 AD, capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century and the largest stone structure in precolonial Southern Africa, built by ancestors of the Shona people.

xhosa-people.name: Xhosa
xhosa-people.summary: A Nguni ethnic group and South Africa's second-largest, native isiXhosa speakers who have inhabited southeastern Southern Africa since around the 7th century.

tsodilo.name: Tsodilo Hills
tsodilo.summary: UNESCO World Heritage site in Botswana with over 4,500 rock paintings and rock shelters, holding deep religious significance to local peoples.
